articles.title: ShiftLens: A System for 3D-Printing Lenticular Objects
articles.summary: Let's say you're designing a switch that must change color when a user activates it. You'd typically think of integrating an LED. But researchers at MIT have developed a low-tech, no-electronics-required way of accomplishing the same. Their process, called ShiftLens , is a way of 3D printing lenticular objects. The idea is that you've got an outer lens layer of transparent material. Beneath that is a pattern layer printed in contrasting colors, in stripes that correspond with the linear lenses of the top layer.
